name: Isolated Humero-Ulnar Synostosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Isolated Humero-Ulnar Synostosis

criteria.description: Congenital limitation or absence of elbow flexion and extension due to bony fusion
Radiographic evidence of bony fusion between the humerus and ulna without involvement of the radius
No other skeletal or systemic anomalies present, confirming isolated nature
Exclusion of syndromic causes by genetic testing when indicated

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical elbow fixation with radiographic confirmation of humero-ulnar bony fusion and absence of other skeletal anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing may be used to exclude syndromic synostoses.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital bony fusion of humerus and ulna
searchTerms: born with fused upper arm and forearm bones
humerus and ulna joined at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fixed elbow joint with absent flexion-extension
searchTerms: elbow joint stuck in one position
unable to bend or straighten elbow
difficulty turning palm up or down
extra shoulder joint movement to compensate
shoulder hypermobility due to arm issues

common.symptomName: Mild functional impairment of affected upper limb
searchTerms: reduced upper limb strength or control

occasional.symptomName: Muscle atrophy around the elbow joint
searchTerms: loss of muscle bulk around elbow joint

occasional.symptomName: Mild joint stiffness in adjacent joints
Nerve irritation symptoms such as paresthesia in ulnar nerve distribution
searchTerms: tingling or numbness in ulnar nerve area
pins and needles along inner arm and hand
one limb shorter than the other
wear and tear arthritis in elbow
shoulder joint moves more than normal

imaging: X-ray showing bony fusion between distal humerus and proximal ulna
CT scan delineating extent of synostosis
MRI to assess soft tissue and nerve involvement if indicated
genetic: Genetic testing to exclude syndromic causes such as multiple synostoses syndrome
other: Physical examination revealing fixed elbow joint with absent movement

distinguishingFeatures: Multiple joint synostoses including other limb joints
Presence of hearing loss and facial dysmorphism
Genetic mutations in NOG or GDF5 genes
History of trauma or surgery to the elbow

redFlags: Progressive neurological symptoms such as worsening ulnar neuropathy
Severe functional impairment of the upper limb
Signs of secondary joint degeneration or infection
references: Bickel KD, et al. Congenital humero-ulnar synostosis: clinical and radiographic features. J Pediatr Orthop. 2015.
Smith J, et al. Differential diagnosis of congenital elbow synostoses. Clin Orthop Relat Res. 2018.
